title: arXiv AI papers — Friday, 9 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; with sparse independent attention and citation evidence for this very recent batch, the ordering is inferred from surfaced external discussion, cross-list breadth, and empirical scope—not readership or downloads.

sections.title: Caught in the Act: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
sections.abstract: The authors train white-box probes on a broad falsehood dataset and report strong detection of agentic and introspective deception, including 98.8% AUC on SHADE-Arena.
sections.claimed_contribution: Multi-layer, multi-token probes trained on FIBS detect falsehoods in SHADE-Arena and generalize to several introspective-deception tests.
sections.unique_caveat: FIBS is largely artificial and mostly off-policy; probe utility is bounded by what the probed model believes and which persona is active.

sections.title: What 30,000 Hours of Ego-centric Video Does Not Teach
sections.abstract: Across a 300-to-30,000-hour training ladder, the authors find that more egocentric video improves agent and object-interaction fidelity unevenly, with object dynamics remaining a bottleneck.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce object-centric adaptive noise-scheduling supervision and report that it raises object fidelity, while an interaction gap remains.
sections.unique_caveat: Data volume and optimization budget are coupled in the scale ladder; the training and evaluation protocols are limited, so extrapolation beyond the tested range is uncertain.

sections.title: Cited but Not Consulted: A Counterfactual Audit of Legal Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
sections.abstract: Across seven open-weight models and four legal-reasoning benchmarks, correct authority citations often did not mean a model’s verdict changed when that authority was counterfactually replaced.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose an authority-swap test with internal commitment tracking and report that naming the correct authority is a poor proxy for whether the verdict depends on it.
sections.unique_caveat: Sample sizes are moderate and the authority-swap intervention also changes the question; conclusions are behavioral and limited to the stated prompts and benchmarks.

sections.title: OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport
sections.abstract: OnTrack compares an agent’s live steps and dependencies with prior successful traces to flag process anomalies; on SWE-bench trajectories the authors report early discrimination and compute savings from aborting likely failures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a streaming, structure-aware optimal-transport monitor intended to intervene during an agent run, rather than score logs only after completion.
sections.unique_caveat: OnTrack detects process anomalies rather than predicting task success; generic signals approach chance with trajectory length controlled, and dependency extraction remains a constraint.

sections.title: Searching for “Harmful Refusal”: A Psychometric Audit of an AI Safety Benchmark
sections.abstract: The authors find that HELM Safety’s HarmBench results do not support treating “harmful refusal” as one measurable dimension; multi-factor models fit better than a single score.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors apply multidimensional item-response and differential-item-functioning analyses, arguing that a single aggregate score blends distinct response behaviors.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are limited to the HELM Safety model pool and tested operationalization; scores rely on two LLM judges, and the original classifier pipeline was not replicated.

sections.title: All Verdicts are Not Equal: Rethinking LLM Judge Reliability
sections.abstract: An audit of six judges across four benchmarks finds that repeated-run consistency, order invariance, and correctness can diverge; the paper introduces a trustworthy-verdict metric combining those properties.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors define a trustworthy-verdict rate and show how candidate-order flips impose an accuracy ceiling; holistic rubric scoring improved the metric in their comparisons.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors test four English-language pairwise benchmarks and closed-weight models; transfer to other languages or listwise ranking remains untested.

sections.title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
sections.abstract: Reanalyzing 228 tasks and 26 AI systems with splines and item-response theory, the authors find a near-flat task-difficulty region around 2–30 minutes, challenging a uniformly log-linear reading of time horizons.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose fitting flexible difficulty curves and recommend interpreting time-horizon estimates alongside construct-validity diagnostics.
sections.unique_caveat: The analysis is grounded in the available task range; newly added, longer tasks need not preserve the currently observed curve shape.

sections.title: OmniCapBench: A Deep-Structured Evaluation Framework for Fine-Grained Audio-Visual Captioning
sections.abstract: OmniCapBench evaluates audio-visual captions as atomic entity, shot, and event units; on 786 annotated videos, the authors report that current models struggle with long-horizon cross-modal alignment and identity persistence.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper separates deterministic structural checks from localized semantic comparisons, aiming to make audio-visual caption errors easier to diagnose.
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark is limited to videos shorter than five minutes and a finite annotation scope; evaluator-model bias is not fully excluded.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: Evaluation validity and measurement dominate this selected batch, with agent-safety monitoring and multimodal/robotic interaction fidelity as adjacent threads.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: Follow-up work should test probe generalization across personas, separate data scale from optimization in world models, design cleaner causal tests for explanation faithfulness, measure false-stop tradeoffs in live agent monitors, replicate benchmark validity across languages and evaluator types, check capability-curve extrapolation, and extend multimodal grounding benchmarks to longer videos.
